notices.name: SpaceX Mission Page
notices.raw:
On Sunday, September 13 at 2:49 p.m. ET, SpaceX launched the SES O3b mPOWER mission to medium Earth orbit from Space Launch Complex 40 (SLC-40) at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. 

This was the 29th flight for the first stage booster supporting this mission, which previously supported Ax-2, Euclid, Ax-3, CRS-30, SES ASTRA 1P, NG-21, and 22 Starlink missions. Following stage separation, the first stage landed on the A Shortfall of Gravitas droneship, which was stationed in the Atlantic Ocean.

notices.name: SpaceX Mission Page
notices.raw:
SpaceX is targeting Thursday, October 1 for Falcon Heavy’s launch of the NROL-97 mission from Launch Complex 39A (LC-39A) at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. Liftoff is targeted for 11:53 p.m. ET, with a backup opportunity available on Friday, October 2 at 11:48 p.m. ET.

A live webcast of the NROL-97 mission will begin about 10 minutes prior to liftoff, which you can watch here and on X @SpaceX. 

This is the second and fourth flight for the two first stage side boosters supporting this mission, which previously launched the GOES-U, Viasat-3 F3, and Roman Space Telescope missions. Following stage separation, Falcon Heavy’s two side boosters will land on SpaceX’s Landing Zones 1 and 2 (LZ-1 and LZ-2) at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida.

notices.name: SpaceX Mission Page
notices.raw:
SpaceX’s Falcon 9 is targeting the launch of 27 Starlink satellites to low-Earth orbit from Space Launch Complex 4 East (SLC-4E) at Vandenberg Space Force Base in California.

A live webcast of this mission will begin about 10 minutes prior to liftoff, which you can watch here and on X @SpaceX. 

This will be the 20th flight for the first stage booster supporting this mission, which previously launched NROL-126, Transporter-12, SPHEREx, NROL-57, USSF-366, and 14 Starlink missions. Following stage separation, the first stage will land on the Of Course I Still Love You droneship, which will be stationed in the Pacific Ocean.

There is the possibility that residents of Santa Barbara, San Luis Obispo, and Ventura counties may hear one or more sonic booms during the launch, but what residents experience will depend on weather and other conditions.

This was the 17th flight for the first stage booster supporting this mission, which previously launched SDA-T1TL-B, SDA-T1TL-C, Transporter-16, and now 14 Starlink missions. There was a possibility that residents of Santa Barbara, San Luis Obispo, and Ventura counties may have heard  one or more sonic booms during the launch, but what residents experienced depended on weather and other conditions.
